On Nov 29, 2026, at 08:27, Jordan Blake wrote:
> Team —
>
> We have an active customer incident with Lumen Health (see thread). Please prioritize. Quick checklist: 

Update from triage: we’re seeing elevated KV cache evictions leading to increased recomputation for long-context requests. A recent micro-deploy at ~06:20 PST changed eviction thresholds on the shard group that serves the Lumen routing policy — likely the trigger. No OOMs observed yet, but GC and CPU share are higher on affected hosts.

Mitigation applied at 08:48 PST: temporarily reverted the eviction threshold change and rebalanced cache shards for the affected pool. Early signal: error rate down from ~15% to ~4% over the last 6 minutes and p95 tail latency reduced by ~40%. Continuing to monitor; keeping the bridge open for 45m.

Will prepare a short exec summary for the customer (draft attached).

Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-29T09:25:00-08:00
Subject: Executive update — stabilization in progress (Lumen Health)

Sara / Michael —

First, apologies for the disruption this morning. Summary and current status below (concise):

What happened
- Starting ~07:45 PST 11/29, a subset of generation requests for redwood/gpt-large-rl that use long context experienced elevated error rates and high tail latency (customer-reported ~15% error impact at peak).

Root cause (preliminary)
- A micro-deploy adjusted KV cache eviction thresholds on the shard group routing Lumen’s traffic. That change increased eviction churn for long-context requests, which increased recomputation and tail latency.

Mitigation completed (09:05 PST)
- Reverted the eviction-threshold change and rebalanced cache shards for the impacted pool. Immediate signals: error rate reduced to ~4% and p95 latency improved ~40%.

Customer impact
- Affected traffic window: ~07:45–09:05 PST. Estimated % of production requests impacted: peak ~15%, now reduced to <5%. No data integrity issues observed.

Next steps
- Full RCA and timeline for a permanent fix (code + test coverage) by 2026-12-03.
- Postmortem meeting scheduled: 2026-12-01T10:00 PST (invite attached).
- We will propose a service credit commensurate with the duration/impact; Neha will send a formal credit estimate within 48 hours.

Attachments / links
- Customer exec brief (v1): customer_exec_brief_v1.pdf
- Bridge recording and logs: https://zoom.us/recording/abc123 (will share once processed)

We understand the timing was poor given your webcast; we’re available for a follow-up briefing. Please let me know if you’d like a short call with our CTO and Head of Runtime.

Again, sincere apologies — we take incidents like this seriously and will both fix the root cause and improve our internal deployment guardrails.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
